title: Affine test algebras admit finite type charts over a prescribed affine cover
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme with an affine open covering $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $V\subseteq X$ be an affine open, put $R=\mathcal O_X(V)$, and let $R\to B$ be a finite type homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Under the canonical identification $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$, write $h:Y=\operatorname{Spec}B\to V$ for its spectrum morphism and $f:Y\to X$ for its composite with the open inclusion [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], both $h$ and $f$ are locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $Y$ is locally Noetherian. There exist a function $i:|Y|\to I$ and affine opens $W_y\subseteq Y$, one for each $y\in Y$, such that $y\in W_y\subseteq f^{-1}(U_{i(y)})$, $Y=\bigcup_{y\in Y}W_y$, and every induced map $\mathcal O_X(U_{i(y)})\to\mathcal O_Y(W_y)$ is of finite type. No finiteness of $I$ or nonemptiness of $Y$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] to the affine open $V$ of the locally Noetherian scheme $X$: its ring $R$ is Noetherian. Since $B$ is a finite type $R$-algebra, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] gives that $B$ is Noetherian. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine and its global section ring is $B$. The affine cover indexed by a singleton whose sole member is all of $Y$ therefore satisfies [pqf-def-locnoeth], so $Y$ is locally Noetherian. This singleton cover is valid even when $B$ is the zero ring and $Y$ is empty.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; algebra.tex Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; properties.tex Tags 01OW and 01OV

proof.text: For every $y\in Y$, apply the reverse implication of [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion] using the source affine open $Y\subseteq Y$ and target affine open $V\subseteq V$. The source open contains $y$ and its image lies in the target open because $h$ has codomain $V$. Under the canonical identification $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$ in the statement and the spectrum construction [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the resulting global-section map is the given finite type homomorphism $R\to B$. These witnesses establish that $h$ is locally of finite type; for empty $Y$ the pointwise criterion is vacuous.

source.place: Tags 01T1 and 01T2, definition-finite-type and lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize; Tag 07R4, lemma-J, finite type test algebra paragraph

proof.text: Let $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ be the open inclusion. It is an immersion: it factors as the identity closed immersion $V\to V$ followed by the open immersion $j$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft] makes $j$ locally of finite type. In clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], substitute $h:Y\to V$ for its first morphism and $j:V\to X$ for its second, and take the locally-of-finite-type alternative. Step 2 supplies the hypothesis on $h$, and the preceding sentence supplies the hypothesis on $j$, so their composite $f=j\circ h$ is locally of finite type.

source.place: Tag 07R4, lemma-J, first paragraph; Tags 01T5 and 01T3, lemma-immersion-locally-finite-type and lemma-composition-finite-type

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$. Since the $U_i$ cover $X$, there exists $a\in I$ with $f(y)\in U_a$. Continuity of the scheme morphism $f$ makes $f^{-1}(U_a)$ an open neighbourhood of $y$. The statement of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], applied to this open neighbourhood, gives an affine open $W$ with $y\in W\subseteq f^{-1}(U_a)$. Thus for every $y$ the set of pairs $(a,W)$ satisfying these conditions is nonempty. Choose one such pair for each $y$, and denote its components by $i(y)$ and $W_y$. This gives one function and one family with the required simultaneous containment; it makes no assertion that an inverse image or an intersection is affine.

source.place: Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens; morphisms.tex Tag 07R4, lemma-J, last paragraph

proof.text: For each $y$, the chosen opens $U_{i(y)}\subseteq X$ and $W_y\subseteq Y$ are affine. If $z\in W_y$, step 4 gives $z\in f^{-1}(U_{i(y)})$, hence $f(z)\in U_{i(y)}$; therefore $f(W_y)\subseteq U_{i(y)}$. Apply the forward implication of [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] to the morphism $f$, locally of finite type by step 3, and this affine pair. It asserts directly that the map $\mathcal O_X(U_{i(y)})\to\mathcal O_Y(W_y)$ induced by $f$ is of finite type, which is the map in the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize, (1) implies (2); Tag 07R4, lemma-J, last paragraph

proof.text: Every $y\in Y$ lies in its own $W_y$, so $Y=\bigcup_{y\in Y}W_y$. Only a pointwise choice was used; the index set $I$ need not be finite. If $Y=\varnothing$, take the empty function $|Y|\to I$ and the empty family of opens. Their union is empty and all pointwise conditions are vacuous, including when $I=\varnothing$.
